traditionalDress.men: Kurta-pajama or kurta with a turban; the turban remains an important part of Punjabi Sikh identity and formal dress for many people.
traditionalDress.women: Salwar kameez, often paired with a dupatta; phulkari textiles are strongly associated with Punjab.

festivals.name: Baisakhi
festivals.description: A spring harvest festival with deep significance in Punjab, accompanied by fairs, music, dance and community gatherings.

festivals.name: Lohri
festivals.description: A winter festival centred on bonfires, seasonal foods, songs and community celebration.

festivals.name: Gurpurab
festivals.description: Sikh commemorative observances honouring the lives and teachings of the Gurus, often marked by prayers, processions and langar.

cuisine: Makki di roti and sarson da saag
folklore: Punjabi oral culture is rich in qisse and sung narratives, alongside devotional poetry and seasonal folk songs. Stories of legendary lovers and folk heroes have long travelled through performance traditions.
